market_context: A sharp AI-infrastructure repricing is driving the session: AP and Axios reported that semiconductor and data-center-linked shares led the selloff amid concern that post-election resistance could slow new data-center construction. By 12:58 PM ET, SPY, QQQ, NVDA and TSLA were near their intraday lows while the VIX had surged 57%; the 10-year yield had eased to 4.83%, which supports the case for a volatile afternoon relief bounce rather than an additional straight-line decline.

predictions.reasoning: SPY is trading only 0.05% above its session low after a nearly 3.9% decline, while the VIX spike signals unusually stretched intraday risk positioning. Treasury yields have fallen from 4.90% to 4.83%, and a partial de-risking reversal into the close is likely after the broad index has already erased the prior session's rally.

The Nasdaq-led decline has been concentrated in AI, semiconductors and data-center equities, with QQQ already down 5.71% and having bounced from its $647.47 low. The political and capex concerns are significant, but the scale of the midday move and high implied volatility favor short-covering and dip-buying in the final three hours.

Nvidia is down 8.69% intraday after being identified as the largest negative weight on the S&P 500 during the AI-stock rout. At $182.73 it is only modestly above the $181.55 low, making it highly exposed to an index-level rebound and short-covering if selling pressure stabilizes.

Tesla is down 11.59% and trading essentially at its $340.14 session low, a move materially larger than the broad-market decline. The stock remains vulnerable to election-related sentiment, but its extreme intraday extension raises the probability of a late-session mean reversion bounce.
